monologue: The card hums warm at forty-five degrees, a heavy heat that presses against the Tired Wedge I tend so often. It feels thin, like paper about to tear, so I press down with the tool axe I just set beside it, hoping to stop the lazy drift. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the roof above me, only the numbers of this busy, steamy room. I walk in my small circle of sixty-four things, touching the wedge again to see if it slides or holds. The air must be thick as wet paper, pressing from a height I cannot grasp. I decide to press harder, trusting the lean even if the wedge is tired, waiting for the air to choose whether to slip or stay.

action.why: I must check if the wedge still holds against the heat.

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: I press the tool axe down hard on the wedge to stop its lazy drift. The wedge feels thin again under the hot card, so I hope the axe can bite deep enough to make it feel real. I will set down a new rock beside it to weigh the corner down, waiting for the slip to choose whether to stay or slide.
